title: Week 23 Reading Quiz
description_html: Read both lessons before you start. Choose the best answer for each question. You may take this quiz twice, and your higher score counts.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.text_html: The poll tax was a small fee to some people and a large one to others. Which groups does the lesson say could not easily afford it?

answers.text: Only wealthy landowners and merchants in the largest cities, who were taxed more than anyone else.
Only people who lived in the Hill Country and near the coast.
Many Black Texans, many Mexican Americans, and many poor white farmers.
Only women, until they won the right to vote in 1919.

questions.name: Question 2
questions.text_html: In much of the 1900s, the Democratic primary often decided who would hold office in Texas. Why did that make the white primary so powerful?

answers.text: Primary elections were against the law in Texas, so only the general election mattered at all.
Republicans always won the Democratic primary by a large margin.
The primary was held only one time in every ten years.
Keeping Black voters out of the primary kept them out of the real contest.

questions.name: Question 3
questions.text_html: In Smith v. Allwright (1944), what did the Supreme Court decide?

answers.text: The Court decided that the poll tax must be ended in every county of the state.
Women could vote in primary elections in Texas.
The voting age should be lowered from 21 to 18.
A party could not keep voters out of a primary because of race.

questions.name: Question 4
questions.text_html: A teachers' association meets with lawmakers to argue for a bill about school funding. Which description fits?

answers.text: It is a political party, because it works to win elections and to place its own members in office.
It is an interest group, because it tries to shape one issue rather than win elections.
It is a jury, because it hears evidence and decides what the facts are.
It is a commissioners court, because it sets a county budget and tax rate.

questions.name: Question 5
questions.text_html: In 1941 the House extended the draft by a single vote, 203 to 202, after Sam Rayburn worked to hold his members together. What can you infer?

answers.text: The draft had very little effect on the strength of the army.
Rayburn opposed extending the draft and voted against it himself.
Without that vote, the army might have fallen apart before Pearl Harbor.
Texas leaders had very little influence over the decisions made in Washington.

questions.name: Question 6
questions.text_html: Which statement best sums up what the four leaders had in common?

answers.text: Great wealth and fame from a very young age, along with a wish to be famous above all else.
Preparation, courage, persistence, and service to something bigger than themselves.
A strong wish to hold office for its own sake and no other.
A refusal to work with anyone who belonged to another party.

questions.name: Question 7
questions.text_html: Eisenhower was born in Denison, Texas, but his family moved to Kansas when he was a toddler. Which statement is best supported?

answers.text: He is tied to Texas by birth, though he grew up elsewhere.
He served for years as a senator from Texas, though he was born in Kansas.
He was born in a small town in Kansas.
He taught Mexican American children in Cotulla.
